interface.name: inox_glass_manager_v1

description.summary: frosted glass (backdrop blur) for a surface

interface.description:
Private, unstable Inox protocol that lets a client ask the compositor to frost part of a surface it draws: the compositor blurs what is already composited *behind* that region and lets the client's translucent pixels blend over the blurred backdrop.
Why this is a compositor-side feature. A client can blur anything it renders itself, but it cannot sample the pixels behind its own surface: those live in the compositor's framebuffer, and no protocol hands them out (that is the whole point of a compositor). A frosted pane that shows the wallpaper and the windows behind it therefore has to be drawn by the component that owns the composited framebuffer, which is the compositor.
What this protocol does *not* grant. The blurred pixels never leave the compositor: a client asks for a region to be blurred and blended, and receives no image, no buffer and no colour back. It learns only whether the compositor accepted the request (through the capabilities event), so this is not a screen-reading capability and cannot be used to observe another client's content. Every request is clipped to the surface it was made for, so a client cannot frost — or force work on — a region of the output it does not draw.
Cost and lifetime. The compositor clamps the requested radius to its own maximum, reports that maximum through capabilities, and applies the effect only while the surface is mapped and committed. Frosting ends when the surface, the glass object or the client goes away, and a compositor that cannot blur (no renderer support, a locked session, a surface whose pixels are not composited at all) simply does not apply it.
Which surfaces can be frosted. The effect needs a surface whose position the compositor knows without waiting for a window-management decision, so this compositor frosts surfaces with a layer role (wlr-layer-shell) — a panel, a dock, a notification stack — and reports max_radius 0 for any other surface, an ordinary toplevel included. A client therefore creates the layer role first and the glass object second; a client that asks earlier is told 0, and may destroy the object and ask again once the role exists. Advertising a maximum the compositor would not honour for that surface is the one thing the event must never do, precisely because the client decides its fallback (plain translucency) from it.
This protocol is an Inox extension and is not part of the upstream wayland-protocols. It is unstable until Inox 1.0: the interface may change in a backwards-incompatible way, and consumers must negotiate through the version event and the capabilities event instead of assuming a fixed revision.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can be done by creating a new version of this protocol.

entry.name: already_created
entry.summary: the surface already has an inox_glass_v1 object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. The glass objects it created stay valid: they belong to the surface they were created for, not to this object.

request.name: get_glass

description.summary: create a glass object for a surface

request.description:
Create a frost controller for `surface`. A surface may have at most one such object; asking for a second one is a protocol error, because two controllers would describe the same pane with conflicting parameters.
The object starts with frosting disabled: a client that creates one and sets nothing has asked for nothing. The compositor sends the capabilities event for this object once it has been created, which is how a client learns the largest radius it accepts before it sets one.

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: the surface whose backdrop should be frosted

interface.name: inox_glass_v1
interface.description:
Parameters for frosting one surface. Every request replaces the previous value; the effect is applied from the next committed frame on.
Coordinates and units. The region is in the surface's own logical coordinates and is clipped to that surface: a region that reaches outside the surface is not an error, the part inside is used, and a region with no area inside the surface means "nothing to frost". The radius is in logical pixels and is clamped to the maximum the compositor reported; 0 means the backdrop is not blurred, which is what a client wants when its glass material must degrade to plain translucency.

request.name: set_radius
request.description: Set the blur radius in logical pixels. Values above the compositor's maximum are clamped to it rather than rejected, so a client that scales its pane can keep asking for "as much as the compositor can do"; 0 disables the blur and leaves the surface composited as an ordinary translucent surface.

request.name: set_region

description.summary: set the region to frost, in surface-local coordinates

request.description:
Set the region to frost, relative to the surface's top-left corner. A width or height that is not positive clears the region, so a client can stop frosting a pane without destroying the object.
The initial region of a new object is empty, so a client that only sets a radius does not silently frost whatever the surface happens to cover.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. Frosting this surface ends with the next committed frame; the surface itself is not touched.

event.name: capabilities
event.description:
Sent once, right after the object is created, before any request on it is answered. `max_radius` is the largest blur radius the compositor will apply, in logical pixels.
A maximum of 0 means this compositor will not blur this surface's backdrop at all — no renderer support, a locked session, or a surface with no layer role, which the compositor does not composite at a known desktop layer. A client must then present its glass as plain translucency instead of claiming a blur it did not get, and it may ask again for a surface that has gained a layer role since.

arg.name: max_radius
arg.summary: largest accepted blur radius, 0 if none
